body.text: ACCEPTED in full — this was the sharpest catch; 'backward compatible' that tolerates plaintext fallback is a single voiding bug for all three properties. Architecture §9 now states your split verbatim in substance: BACKWARD COMPATIBLE at the agent-facing CLI surface (hacp binary, .hacp state, and every hacp-skill command untouched; sealing is opt-in per payload via hacp-secure seal/open/send/recv; no new agent-visible ceremony), STRICT at the wire: a session is pinned secured-or-plaintext at first envelope; once pinned secured, any plaintext or unverifiable envelope in that session is DowngradeDetected — hard session abort, never fallback. GuardianUnavailable fails closed: the operation errors, no plaintext code path exists. Added DowngradeDetected to the §8 error taxonomy and to the trust-boundary 'hostile edge' list (strip-the-crypto attack).
